LESSON: IMITATIVE SPEAKING: PHONETIC AWARENESS MODELING ENGAGEMENT PRONUNCIATION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: FRENCH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.9: Imitative speaking: Phonetic awareness Modeling Engagement Pronunciation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Imitative speaking: Phonetic awareness Modeling Engagement Pronunciation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do you engage your listener in oral communication?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify vocabulary and expressions from audio stimuli
2. imitate pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from source
3. show enthusiasm towards speaking activities

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: IMITATIVE SPEAKING: PHONETIC AWARENESS MODELING ENGAGEMENT PRONUNCIATION
Subject: FRENCH · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Imitative speaking: Phonetic awareness Modeling Engagement Pronunciation helps you succeed in FRENCH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: IMITATIVE SPEAKING: PHONETIC AWARENESS MODELING ENGAGEMENT PRONUNCIATION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify vocabulary and expressions from audio stimuli

What this means
In this part you learn to identify vocabulary and expressions from audio stimuli. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify vocabulary and expressions from audio stimuli.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Imitative speaking: Phonetic awareness Modeling Engagement Pronunciation”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify vocabulary and expressions from audio stimuli. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Imitate pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from source

What this means
In this part you learn to imitate pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from source. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: imitate pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from source.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Imitative speaking: Phonetic awareness Modeling Engagement Pronunciation to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can imitate pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from source. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Show enthusiasm towards speaking activities

What this means
In this part you learn to show enthusiasm towards speaking activities. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: show enthusiasm towards speaking activities.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can show enthusiasm towards speaking activities. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Imitative speaking: Phonetic awareness Modeling Engagement Pronunciation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Imitative speaking: Phonetic awareness Modeling Engagement Pronunciation”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify vocabulary and expressions from audio stimuli)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Imitative speaking: Phonetic awareness Modeling Engagement Pronunciation to a partner. (skill: imitate pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from source)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: show enthusiasm towards speaking activities)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Imitative speaking: Phonetic awareness Modeling Engagement Pronunciation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify vocabulary and expressions from audio stimuli.
3. Practise this skill: imitate pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from source.
4. Practise this skill: show enthusiasm towards speaking activities.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Imitative speaking: Phonetic awareness Modeling Engagement Pronunciation from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Imitative speaking: Phonetic awareness Modeling Engagement Pronunciation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Imitative speaking: Phonetic awareness Modeling Engagement Pronunciation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you engage your listener in oral communication?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Imitative speaking: Phonetic awareness Modeling Engagement Pronunciation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify vocabulary and expressions from audio stimuli.
5. Be able to: imitate pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from source.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
